title: Wah-wah fail
prompt:
A 2.8-second comedic "wah-wah" fail for the plan-goes-wrong beat, 134,400 samples, 30 fps, first note on frame 0. Muted-brass feel: band-limited additive saw with a slight pitch scoop into each note, a breathy noise onset, and a plunger-mute "wah": a resonant band-pass sweeping ~500 -> 1,400 -> 500 Hz on each note. The last note holds and droops ~40 cents with a widening vibrato as it fades to true silence by ~2.6 s. Small dry room, no reverb wash. Mono-ish, low end centred. ORIGINAL melody: do NOT use the stock four-note descending-semitone 'sad trombone' figure (e.g. Bb-A-Ab-G or any four equal falling semitone steps); write the contour given in the take angle.

Take angle 1 (three-step droop): three notes: E4 (frame 0, short), C#4 (frame 12, short), then C4 (frame 26) held with a long downward bend of about a minor third over its last second, plunger wah opening and closing twice on the held note.
notes:
Original three-step droop, not the stock four-semitone sad trombone: E4 (frame 0), C#4 (frame 12), then a held C4 (frame 26) that bends down a minor third to A3 with a widening vibrato, the plunger mute opening and closing twice.
Band-limited additive saw with the plunger band-pass (500→1,400→500 Hz) applied per harmonic, a pitch scoop and breath noise on each note, small dry room, near mono; true silence by ~2.6 s.
Take 1 of 3, picked as the clearest "plan went wrong" beat; synthesised brass may read a touch kazoo-ish.
